### Summary

A hydrostatic primitive-equation core is a dynamical core that replaces the vertical momentum equation by
hydrostatic balance, so that the vertical velocity is diagnosed instead of predicted and vertically propagating
sound waves are filtered out. That definition is general background, not a fact of the code at the pin; it is given
so that a reader who has used such a core can see what changes. snapy instead solves the compressible equations of
@sec-ch02-laws. This section lists, as facts of the code at the pin, the points where a reader of that background
meets a difference, each with the section that states it.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Lists where the equations and numerics at the pin differ from a hydrostatic core (@tbl-ch02-pecore).

**Data.** N/A, a comparison; it reads no state.

**Placement.** N/A; each difference sits in the section the table cites.

**Activation.** None; the compressible equations are always solved.

**Guarantee / limits.** No comparison run against any other model is made at the pin.

**Evidence.** The sections and code of @tbl-ch02-pecore and @tbl-ch02-pecore-code.
:::

| question | snapy at the pin | where |
|---|---|---|
| Is the vertical velocity prognostic? | Yes: the vertical momentum is a conserved row, updated by its flux divergence and sources like the other momenta. | @sec-ch02-laws |
| Where does pressure come from? | From the equation of state of each cell's conserved state, not from integrating a hydrostatic column. | @sec-ch02-interface |
| Is pressure the vertical coordinate? | No: $x_1$ is a fixed height or radius; there is no pressure, sigma or hybrid coordinate. | @sec-appa-conventions |
| Are sound waves in the solution? | Yes: the explicit step is bounded by $\lvert v\rvert+c_s$ in every direction. | @sec-ch07-cfl |
| Can the vertical sound-wave bound be removed? | Yes, by the vertically implicit correction, which acts in $x_1$ only and needs the whole column on one rank. | @sec-ch07-vic-options |
| Is there a hydrostatic switch? | `non-hydrostatic`[^rg-0dd1d9434f28] below 1 replaces part of gravity by the cell's own pressure difference; even at 0 the vertical velocity stays prognostic. | @sec-ch05-hsmode |
| Is the geometry shallow? | No: on the spherical grids every metric quantity uses the radius of its own cell; gravity is one constant, `grav1`. | @sec-ch03-sphpolar, @sec-ch06-cell |
| Is the Coriolis force traditional? | Not by default: the full rotation vector is used; `traditional: true` keeps its radial part, on the cubed sphere only. | @sec-ch09-coriolis |

: Where snapy at the pin differs from a hydrostatic primitive-equation core. {#tbl-ch02-pecore}

### Derivation

N/A: the section compares, it derives nothing. The equations are those of @sec-ch02-laws.

### Numerical method

N/A: no scheme of its own. The consequence that matters most in practice is the time step: an explicit
compressible step is limited by the sound speed in $x_1$ as well as in $x_2$ and $x_3$, which is why the vertically
implicit correction exists (@sec-ch07).

: Code map of the differences. {#tbl-ch02-pecore-code}

**How to use it.** A deck ported from a hydrostatic core needs a geometric $x_1$ grid (@sec-ch03-globalgrid), an
initial state in hydrostatic balance on that grid (@sec-ch05-balcol), and either a time step under the vertical
acoustic bound or `integration/implicit-scheme` (@sec-ch07-vic-options). Refused: none here; the keys are
refused where their own sections say.

### Tests

N/A: the comparison asserts nothing of its own. The tests are those of the cited sections.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- No run of snapy against a hydrostatic core, and no measured cost of the compressible step against one, exists at
  the pin.
:::

The table lists differences of the equations and the numerics only. Differences of physics packages (radiation,
convection schemes) are not listed; the forcing modules snapy has are the subject of @sec-ch09.

[^rg-0dd1d9434f28]: non-hydrostatic — fraction of the vertical body force retained by the non-hydrostatic treatment
